mechanism: Vasospasm of digital arteries leading to reduced blood flow, causing pallor, cyanosis, and then rubor upon reperfusion. Triggered by cold or stress.
visual_features: Sharp demarcation between affected and unaffected skin
Possible pallor before cyanosis (not visible in this image, but typical)
clinical_context: Episodic color changes in the digits, typically triggered by cold exposure or emotional stress. Can be primary or secondary to an underlying autoimmune condition.

mechanism: Persistent cyanosis of the extremities due to small vessel vasospasm and reduced blood flow. Unlike Raynaud's, it is usually painless and persistent.
visual_features: Absence of distinct color changes (pallor, cyanosis, rubor)
clinical_context: Chronic, painless cyanosis of the extremities, often exacerbated by cold, but present even in warmer conditions. Usually benign but can be associated with underlying conditions.

mechanism: Sudden blockage of an artery supplying the hand, leading to ischemia and potentially tissue necrosis. Can be caused by thrombus, embolus, or trauma.
visual_features: Pain (not directly visible but clinically relevant)
clinical_context: Sudden onset of pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, and poikilothermia in the affected limb. Requires immediate intervention to restore blood flow.

mechanism: Autoimmune disease causing fibrosis and vascular abnormalities, including Raynaud's phenomenon and digital ischemia due to thickening of blood vessel walls and reduced blood flow.
visual_features: Skin thickening (not directly visible but would be present on exam)
Digital ulcers (may or may not be present)
clinical_context: Progressive autoimmune disease affecting the skin and internal organs. Raynaud's phenomenon is often an early manifestation, followed by skin thickening and other systemic symptoms.

mechanism: Atherosclerosis leading to narrowing of arteries supplying the extremities, resulting in reduced blood flow and ischemia. Can cause chronic cyanosis or acute worsening with cold exposure.
clinical_context: Chronic condition characterized by reduced blood flow to the extremities due to atherosclerosis. Can present with claudication, rest pain, and non-healing ulcers. Cyanosis may be present chronically or worsen with cold exposure.
